Every reward-to-risk ratio, stop-ATR distance and break-even hit rate in this report was recomputed from the final entry, target and downside at synthesis rather than carried over from the notes; all ten reproduce the captured figure to two decimals and all ten clear their floors. READ THE RATIO CLUSTERING AS A WARNING. Eight of ten ratios sit between 2.00 and 2.36 against a 2.0 swing floor — the signature CLAUDE.md warns about. Two things make it less damning than it looks and one makes it worse. Six of the ten are amendments to positions whose levels predate today, so the ratio was not fitted this morning; and both stops moved today were moved OUTWARD to clear the ATR floor (CEG 250->241, DINO 97.75->97.00), which is the honest direction. But CEG's target was simultaneously raised 320->340, which is what preserved a 2.19 ratio through a wider stop, and 340 is above CEG's 120-day high of 328.80 — the research notes concede this and do not answer it. Treat CEG's upside as the least defended number in the report. IWM is the thinnest clearance anywhere: a 1.88 ATR stop against the 1.8 ETF floor, and a 266.00 target that is 1.6% BELOW its own 120-day low of 270.36, so it is the one target today that is a projection rather than ground already traded. PRICES: every quote is the 2026-10-08 regular-session close, fetched from finnhub during pre-market. At this hour that is the freshest honest equity price, not stale data — but no idea here is priced off a live 10-09 tape, and the pre-market reaction to Delta's print was not visible when the AAL level was set. SOURCES THAT FAILED, and what each cost: yahoo chart API HTTP 429 on every symbol — no index, VIX, DXY, gold or WTI quote, and no crypto history; yahoo options API HTTP 401 — so market_data.py implied was unusable and NO TARGET IN THIS REPORT WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE OPTIONS-IMPLIED MOVE, a check that normally gates every level; api.nasdaq.com short interest read timeout — no crowding read anywhere, which specifically leaves the AAL short's crowding unmeasured; kalshi via events returned zero markets for CPI, shutdown, recession and Bitcoin; finnhub refuses index CFDs on this plan, so the index gap could not be filled from the fallback; WebSearch found no dated 2026-10-08 market wrap, so the session narrative above is read off fetched prices rather than quoted from coverage. Three event contracts already on the book (KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25, KXFEDDECISION-26SEP-H0, KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5) are left unresolved deliberately rather than restated at a price nobody fetched; the 26SEP contract names a September event and has very likely already settled. That is the correlation cap exactly, and it is why OXY at 60.28 was rejected despite being a reasonable idea. Read those three as one position with three expressions. recommendations.thesis: UPDATE TO AN EXISTING POSITION, not a new idea: opened 2026-08-15 at 63.90, last 65.24 (+2.1%), and the entry, target and stop are all unchanged. The 2026-10-08 session confirmed the thesis - XLE closed +2.97% on a day SPY fell 0.42% and SMH fell 2.84%, reclaiming both the 20d SMA (63.31) and the 50d (62.55) in one move. This morning it was confirmed a second time from the opposite side of the trade, in a filing: Delta disclosed that the benefit from owning a refinery went from the 5c per gallon assumed in July, to 13c realised in the September quarter, to approximately 40c guided for the December quarter. That is a fuel buyer quantifying the crack spread widening eightfold in nine months.
recommendations.key_risk: The move is crack-spread driven, so it is a downstream margin story XLE only partly owns - the index is majority integrated and E&P, and a crude retreat would hit those weights while leaving refining margin intact. A close back below the 50d SMA at 62.55 breaks the setup well before the 60.80 stop does. Note also that the Delta evidence is a disclosure about fuel cost, not a forecast of crude: it confirms margin is being transferred to refiners today and says nothing about how long that lasts. And this is one of three ideas in today's report on a single driver (with DINO long and AAL short), which is the correlation cap - nothing further should be added on crack spreads.
recommendations.counter_argument: XLE sits 1.41% off its 120-day high of 66.17 and has given everything back on a 1-month basis (-0.11% vs SPY +1.51%), so this is the third run at the same ceiling since mid-September rather than a breakout. The answer is that the first two attempts (09-14 high 66.05, 09-15 high 66.12) failed with the sector moving alone; this one comes with the whole downstream complex up 3-5% in a session, which is a different quality of bid. RED TEAM, added: nothing on this page defends the 70.50 target, and fetched 500-session history says it is not a reclaim of old ground — XLE's range over 500 sessions is 37.245 to 66.17, so 70.50 is a two-year high, and 5.26 of the trade's 6.60 of reward (80%) sits above a 66.17 ceiling that has turned price back three times since mid-September. The target is deliberately NOT moved, in either direction: pulling it in to tidy the chart would be as dishonest as pushing it out, and measured to 66.17 this is 0.73:1. Read the 2.13:1 as the ratio to a level XLE has never closed at, and take something off into 66. The position is held because the driver is quantified in an unrelated counterparty's filing and because the 2.36 ATR stop is the only one in the energy cluster clear of the comfort band — not because 70.50 is defended. Conviction cut 5 -> 4: the `positioning` and `counter_argument_answered` items are both the 2026-10-08 session tape, so the four kinds are three facts.

recommendations.thesis: RE-PITCH at an unchanged 13.35 of a short published 2026-10-03 that never filled; what is new is that the thesis was tested this morning and passed. Delta reported September-quarter results before the open on 2026-10-09: adjusted EPS $1.72 against its own July guide of $2.00-$2.50 and consensus of $1.96-$2.01, and operating margin 9.4% against a guide of 11%-13%. Demand was not the problem - revenue grew 16% on flat capacity with TRASM +15% and accelerating. The problem was entirely fuel: $3.61 per gallon, up 60% year-over-year, against the ~$3.15 the guide had assumed off a July 2 forward curve. Delta then guided December-quarter fuel to ~$4.25 per gallon, another ~18% sequentially, and cut full-year EPS to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50. That is an industry cost shock that is accelerating, disclosed by the sector's strongest operator, and American is the major least able to absorb it: most leveraged balance sheet, thinnest operating margin, least premium-cabin mix.
recommendations.key_risk: Shorting requires margin and the loss is unbounded. The sharpest risk is that the read-across is directional, not arithmetic - Delta's revenue grew 16% and is guided to +20%, so the market may look straight through fuel to a demand story, and airlines can rally on a quarter like this. American's network, hedge book and fuel mix are its own and Delta's miss does not compute AAL's. Crowding is unmeasured: market_data.py short timed out against nasdaq this morning, so the assumption that this is already a consensus short is an assumption. The 14.30 stop is 11.6% above the entry on a 3.54% daily ATR, and AAL reports its own Q3 later in October, inside the horizon. RED TEAM, added: conviction cut 5 -> 4. Delta's earnings release and its 8-K cover page are one filing (accession 000002790426000035) cited under two evidence kinds, so this rests on three distinct confirmations, not four. And the catalyst is now BEHIND us — Delta printed at 06:30 ET, so by the opening bell the fuel read-across is the most-written story on the tape, while the one measurement that would show whether it is already positioned (short interest) failed to fetch. Every figure in the thesis was re-read against the SEC filing this morning and verified: adjusted EPS $1.72, adjusted fuel $3.61/gal 'up 60 percent year-over-year', 13c refinery benefit, Q4 guided to ~$4.25/gal with ~$0.40 benefit, FY2026 cut to $5.10-$5.60. Two figures are NOT in that release and are second-hand from the July guide: the $2.00-$2.50 quarter guide and the $6.50-$7.50 prior full-year range. Direction and magnitude are confirmed; those two are not primary.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that at 12.80 AAL is already 31.88% off its 120-day high and the fuel story is priced. Delta's filing answers that with a number rather than an argument. Delta's Q4 guidance carries a refinery benefit of approximately $0.40 per gallon, up from 13c realised in Q3 and the 5c assumed in July - Delta owns a refinery and is therefore partially LONG the crack spread that is squeezing the industry. It captured that offset, posted +15% TRASM on flat capacity, and still cut its full year by 22%. American owns no refinery and captures none of it. So the best-hedged, best-mix operator in the sector sets the floor for how bad this is, not the ceiling. Mechanically, the order also sits 4.3% ABOVE the last price, so it only fills on a bounce - if the thesis really is priced, the trade costs nothing because it never executes.

Summit's BLA for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated non-squamous NSCLC was accepted for filing in January 2026 and carries an FDA PDUFA goal date of November 14, 2026 - 36 days out, stated in the company's own 8-K. In the same filing Summit reported HARMONi-6 interim overall survival of 27.89 months against 23.69 for tislelizumab plus chemotherapy, stratified HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.50-0.87, p=0.0017) and a 24-month OS rate of 64.7% versus 48.6%, so the molecule has produced a statistically significant survival benefit in a Phase III setting. And insiders bought $103.6m of stock on the open market in six transactions over six months with zero sales: chairman Robert Duggan and co-CEO Mahkam Zanganeh each took 3,810,000 shares at $13.12 on 2026-06-12.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a binary and the stop is close to cosmetic - a complete response letter on 2026-11-14 gaps SMMT 30-50% overnight straight through 14.40, and the realised loss will be far past the 2.70 risked. That is the whole reason size is 1% and the tier is lottery rather than the 4-5% conviction 5 would otherwise imply: the sizing is set by the payoff shape, not by the evidence count. Daily ATR is 7.27%, among the widest in the report. Secondary risk: the approval, if it comes, is in a post-TKI EGFR-mutant niche, and a rival threat to the commercial opportunity is live. RED TEAM, added: the 2.19:1 and the +0.28R expectancy in the validation block do not describe this trade. Both are computed off a 14.40 stop the idea itself calls cosmetic, and a complete response letter gaps straight through it — the real left tail is far past the 2.70 risked, so the ratio measures nothing. Size this as a 1% position you are willing to lose whole, not as a 2.19:1.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is the one reading the primary document actually surfaced, and most readers will get it backwards. The spectacular data above is HARMONi-6 - a single-region, multi-centre Phase III conducted entirely in China, in a different population - and it is NOT the dataset the FDA is reviewing. The BLA rests on HARMONi, and third-party coverage reports that statistical significance was not achieved in HARMONi's Western subgroup, leaving the FDA's reading of a directional survival trend (16.8 vs 14.0 months overall; 17.5 vs 14.0 in the Western subgroup as of June 2026) as the live question. Separately, the HARMONi-3 squamous interim PFS analysis showed no early efficacy signal. So the honest statement of this trade is: a coin flip on the FDA's tolerance for a directional trend, taken because three insiders put $103.6m behind it at $13.12 and the asset has proven itself elsewhere - not because the pivotal data is clean. It is not. RED TEAM, added: conviction cut 5 -> 3, and the counter-argument above is verified rather than taken on trust. The 8-K was read this morning: it states the PDUFA goal date of November 14, 2026, it describes HARMONi-6 verbatim as 'a single region, multi-center, Phase III study conducted in China', and the BLA it names rests on HARMONi. So the spectacular OS numbers carrying most of the thesis paragraph are from a trial the FDA is not reviewing. That same filing is cited twice, once as `primary_document` and once as `dated_catalyst`, so the four 'independent kinds' are three at most — and once the HARMONi-6 data is set aside, what actually backs the long is one insider cluster and one technical level. A conviction 5 cannot sit above the sentence 'not because the pivotal data is clean. It is not.' The insider cluster is the real evidence here and it is worth 1%.

The filing also states plainly that HARMONi-6 is a single-region study conducted in China and reports no Western subgroup - which is why the counter_argument above exists

This is not a spin-off trade - the planned separation into Global Taste Elevation and North American Grocery was paused on 2026-02-11 and is still paused. It is a turnaround trade with the owner alongside: new CEO Steve Cahillane paused the split to stop paying dis-synergies, committed $600m to reinvestment and a further $100m to marketing in August, and on 2026-05-12 bought 213,106 shares on the open market for $5.0m at $23.46 - above where the stock trades today. Meanwhile capital has started leaving the AI complex for exactly this kind of de-rated cash generator: XLP was the second-best sector on 2026-10-08 and KHC rose 2.24% from 7% above its 500-day low.

One good staples session is not a trend: KHC is 19.97% below its 120-day high with price under both the 20d SMA (23.49) and the 50d (24.62), and it has gone down through every prior bounce. The 21.20 stop sits only 0.17 above the 500-day low of 21.035 - if that floor breaks there is no support beneath it and no level in 500 sessions to measure the next one against. RED TEAM, added: the 5.0:1 is not a 15-session ratio. The 32.00 target is 16.8 ATR and +39% from the 23.00 entry against a 6.0 ATR guide for a swing — a multi-quarter level wearing a swing label, so the horizon is the number that is wrong, not the target (32.00 sits below the verified 500-day high of 36.31, and the 3.36 ATR stop is genuinely clear of the band, so neither is an artifact). The label is deliberately left alone: relabelling this long_term would switch off both the target-feasibility and the stop-distance checks rather than answer them. Read the ratio as what the turnaround pays over several quarters, not as a two-week proposition. Conviction cut 4 -> 3 because the `counter_argument_answered` evidence IS the `positioning` evidence — both are Cahillane's 2026-05-12 purchase — so there are two distinct confirmations, not three.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the catalyst was cancelled: a company that announced a breakup to unlock value, then shelved it thirteen months later while sales deteriorated, is a value trap and the 42% implied upside is the trap talking. The answer is not an argument, it is a transaction - Cahillane bought $5.0m of stock three months AFTER announcing the pause, at $23.46, with full knowledge of what he had just shelved and what the trajectory looked like. That is the one public signal executives only send in one direction, and it is above today's price.
